_comment: NU Map maintenance schedule. Empty windows = nothing scheduled = the app says nothing.
AN ORDINARY PUSH TO MAIN NEEDS NOTHING HERE. index.html's recovery screen already
handles the one visible effect (a tab left on a stale shell). This file is only for
when THE SITE COMES OFF.
DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Use the Maintenance panel on /northeastern/dev, or:
npm run maint -- outage --start "..." --expect 8h --write
and while it is running: `maint -- extend 6h`, `maint -- done`.
See docs/maintenance.md. The CLI validates with the same code the app runs, so it
cannot write something the browser would silently drop or demote.
One window looks like this:
"end": "2026-08-30T08:00:00Z",         <- DEADLINE: we recover here, no deploy needed
"expectedEnd": "2026-08-30T07:00:00Z", <- optional FORECAST: what we tell people
"severity": "notice" | "degraded" | "offline",
"kind": "deploy" | "data" | "migration" | "infra" | "other",
"features": ["claude", "share", "ratings", "translation", "catalog"],
"backup": false | "optional" | "recommended",
"announceHours": 24, "imminentMinutes": 30, "restoredHours": 2,
"hardBlock": false }
`end` and `expectedEnd` are two different promises and neither can do the other's job.
`end` is the guarantee — the site turns itself back on there even if every deploy fails,
which is why ONE deploy covers a whole event and nothing has to be flipped off after.
`expectedEnd` is the number we quote; once it passes, every surface says "taking longer
than expected" instead of counting down to a time that has gone. For an outage of
unknown length, quote hours and guarantee days.
A file we cannot read or cannot parse means 'nothing scheduled' — this feature can
never be the reason the app is down.
